blocks.text: SUBIC BAY FREEPORT — From a former American naval base that was preserved by thousands of Filipino volunteers to an economic zone employing nearly 177,000 workers, the Subic Bay Freeport has undergone a major transformation in the 34 years since the establishment of the Subic Bay Metropolitan Authority (SBMA). The Freeport’s workforce reached 176,847 as of September, up from 164,400 in 2024, reflecting continued hiring among its 4,744 registered businesses, the SBMA said in a statement on Thursday (November 26).
